svg.text: Registry baseline: what the default toolchain protects
Ecosystem defaults from primary sources, verified 14 Oct 2026 · not part of the trust score · snapshot 25 Oct 2026, 18:32 UTC

g.text: Immutable versionsOnce published, can a version's files never be replaced or added to?
Install checks hashDoes the default client check each download against the registry's hash?
Lockfile pins hashesDoes the default lockfile record artifact hashes, so later installs get identical bytes?
Client checks signatureDoes the default client check a signature or transparency log, so a compromised registry or mirror is detected?
Scoped, expiring tokensCan publish credentials be limited to specific packages and made to expire?
No code at installDoes installing or building leave dependency code unexecuted by default?

rect.title: PyPI · Immutable versions: yes (since Jul 2026). Filenames can never be reused; new files are rejected on releases older than 14 days (before: any release could gain new files).
PyPI · Install checks hash: yes. pip checks each file against the sha256 the index lists for it, without needing --require-hashes.
PyPI · Lockfile pins hashes: partial. pip has no default lockfile; PEP 751 pylock.toml (2025) and tools like uv and Poetry record hashes.
PyPI · Client checks signature: no. PEP 458 (TUF-signed index) is not deployed; PEP 740 attestations are not verified by pip.
PyPI · Scoped, expiring tokens: partial. API tokens can be scoped to one project but never expire (trusted publishing tokens do).
PyPI · No code at install: partial. Wheels run no code; source distributions run their build backend.
npm · Immutable versions: yes. A version number can never be reused, even after unpublishing.
npm · Install checks hash: yes. Tarballs are checked against dist.integrity.
npm · Lockfile pins hashes: yes. package-lock.json records each package's integrity hash.
npm · Client checks signature: no. Registry signatures are checked only by an explicit `npm audit signatures`.
npm · Scoped, expiring tokens: yes (since Nov 2025). Granular tokens only; write tokens expire after at most 90 days, classic tokens were revoked.
npm · No code at install: yes (since Jul 2026). npm 12 runs no dependency install scripts unless allowed (before: all ran).
crates.io · Immutable versions: yes. Versions are yanked, not replaced; deletion only within 72 h or for barely-used single-owner crates.
crates.io · Install checks hash: yes. Cargo checks every .crate against the index's sha256 (cksum).
crates.io · Lockfile pins hashes: yes. Cargo.lock records each crate's checksum.
crates.io · Client checks signature: no. The index is not signed; TUF signing is an open Rust project goal.
crates.io · Scoped, expiring tokens: yes. Tokens can be scoped by endpoint and crate, with an optional expiry.
crates.io · No code at install: no. Dependencies' build scripts and procedural macros run at build time.
RubyGems · Immutable versions: yes. A version cannot be pushed twice, even after it is yanked.
RubyGems · Install checks hash: yes. Bundler validates gems against the compact index's checksums.
RubyGems · Lockfile pins hashes: partial. Gemfile.lock CHECKSUMS since Bundler 2.6, opt-in (bundle lock --add-checksums).
RubyGems · Client checks signature: no. Signed-gem verification is opt-in (gem install -P MediumSecurity); signing is rarely used.
RubyGems · Scoped, expiring tokens: yes. API keys have per-action and per-gem scopes, with an optional expiry.
RubyGems · No code at install: partial. Pure-Ruby gems run nothing; native extensions run extconf.rb on install.
Go · Immutable versions: yes. The proxy and checksum database pin each version's contents; re-tagging upstream changes nothing.
Go · Install checks hash: yes. Every module is checked against go.sum and the checksum database.
Go · Lockfile pins hashes: yes. go.sum records each module's hash.
Go · Client checks signature: yes. The go command checks every module against the signed sum.golang.org log by default.
Go · Scoped, expiring tokens: n/a. No publish credentials exist.
Go · No code at install: yes. An explicit design goal: neither fetching nor building runs dependency code.
Maven Central · Immutable versions: yes. Released components can never be changed or deleted.
Maven Central · Install checks hash: partial. Maven 3 checks .sha1 files but only warns on mismatch by default; Maven 4 fails. The checksums come from the same server as the artifact.
Maven Central · Lockfile pins hashes: no. Maven has no lockfile; third-party plugins exist.
Maven Central · Client checks signature: no. Maven does not check PGP signatures; a plugin is needed.
Maven Central · Scoped, expiring tokens: partial. User tokens can be given an expiry; no per-namespace scoping is documented.
Maven Central · No code at install: partial. Dependency jars are not run, but javac ran classpath annotation processors implicitly until JDK 23; build plugins run by the project's choice.

Packagist · Immutable versions: yes (since Jul 2026). Stable versions keep their original commit when the tag is moved upstream; dev branches stay mutable. Archives are still generated by the forge, so bytes may differ for the same commit.
Packagist · Install checks hash: no. Packagist publishes an empty dist.shasum for forge-hosted archives, so Composer has nothing to check; the commit in the archive URL is the only pin.
Packagist · Lockfile pins hashes: partial. composer.lock pins the commit, but the archive hash is empty for forge-hosted packages.
Packagist · Client checks signature: no. There is nothing signed to check.
Packagist · Scoped, expiring tokens: n/a. Nothing is uploaded; tokens only trigger re-indexing.
Packagist · No code at install: yes. Only the root project's scripts run; dependency plugins need explicit allow-plugins (Composer 2.2+).

svg.text: "since" marks a value that changed recently, so the backfill quarters predate it. Hover a cell for the note; sources in baseline.md.
